target.emptyBody: Add a Spark from the fleet rail first. Benchmarks run against the LLM server on a Spark, or on a Remote endpoint you type in.
target.enterHost: Enter the host of the LLM endpoint to benchmark.
target.remoteTitle: Benchmark another LLM endpoint instead of a Spark's
target.modelTitle: Model currently served on this port
target.remoteHint: On-demand endpoint: nothing is probed until you run. Remote units use LAN HTTP, or an SSH tunnel to loopback if the server only listens on 127.0.0.1.
target.offlineBody: Bring it back online to benchmark its LLM, or switch the target to Remote and point at another endpoint. Saved runs below are still readable.
target.workerBody: and serves no LLM of its own, so nothing can run here. Saved runs below are still readable.
target.noLlmBody: {{error}}Start a model on this Spark (Models panel on its page), check the LLM port in its settings, or switch the target to Remote. Saved runs below are still readable.

error.noServer: No model server was found. Start the model on this Spark (or set a base URL) and try again.
error.connectionFailed: The tool could not reach the model server. Check the URL, the port and that the server is running.
error.noModels: The server answered but lists no models. Load a model first, or set the model name explicitly.
error.authFailed: The server rejected the API key. Enter the right key or save one for this port.
error.modelNotFound: The server does not serve that model name. Leave the model empty to auto-detect it.

notes.toolChoiceOne: This model server does not support forced tool calls (tool_choice "required"), so the scenario that needs it was left out of the score ({{scenarios}}). The run is fine; the score covers the other scenarios, so it is not directly comparable with a server that supports it.
notes.toolChoiceMany: This model server does not support forced tool calls (tool_choice "required"), so the scenarios that need it were left out of the score ({{scenarios}}). The run is fine; the score covers the other scenarios, so it is not directly comparable with a server that supports it.
notes.excludedOne: {{scenarios}} was left out of the score by the tool (see the raw output for the reason).
notes.excludedMany: {{scenarios}} were left out of the score by the tool (see the raw output for the reason).

form.apiKeySaved: Using the key saved for this port

form.apiKeyHintSaved: , and one is saved for this port
form.apiKeyHintTail: . A typed key is only sent together with a base URL, and then goes to the Spark through its environment for this run only and is never stored in this browser.
form.advancedHelp: Every other option of tool-eval-bench, so nothing is out of reach. Options this page sets for you are left out.
form.extraHint: Free-form flags passed through as separate arguments (no shell). Handy for options newer than this form. Flags that sparkDash controls (--json, --probe, …) are refused.

setup.checkFailedTitle: Could not check the Tool Eval Bench install
setup.upgradeNote: This runs uv tool upgrade on {{name}}: it fetches the newest tool-eval-bench from GitHub (SeraphimSerapis/tool-eval-bench) and replaces the installed copy. If uv did not install the current copy, it reinstalls from GitHub instead. Tick force reinstall to reinstall from scratch instead.
setup.installNote: This runs uv tool install from GitHub (SeraphimSerapis/tool-eval-bench) on {{name}}, as the user sparkDash connects with.
setup.needsInternet: It downloads Python packages and needs internet access on that Spark. Nothing is installed on the machine running sparkDash.
setup.uvMissingTitle: uv is not installed on this Spark
setup.uvMissingBody: Installation uses uv. Install it first (curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh on the Spark), then check again.
setup.uvNotFound: uv was not found on the Spark. Install uv first, then try again.
setup.installFailedHint: See the output above for the reason (no internet, a missing Python, a full disk…).
setup.jobRunning: Another Tool Eval Bench job is running on this Spark.
setup.notInstalledTitle: Tool Eval Bench is not installed on {{name}}
setup.lead: This page drives the external tool-eval-bench CLI, which runs on the Spark itself. Install it once and every Tool Eval Bench page becomes available. You can still configure and preview a run meanwhile; Start is disabled until it is installed.
setup.unreachable: The Spark could not be reached
setup.updateUnknown: Could not tell if there is an update
setup.noCommit: The installed version does not name a commit, so it cannot be compared with GitHub.
setup.workDir: Where results live: each run keeps its files under {{path}} on {{name}}; sparkDash also caches finished results so history stays readable when the Spark is off.
setup.upgradedFrom: tool-eval-bench on {{name}} went from {{from}} to {{to}}. You can run a benchmark now.
setup.reinstalled: tool-eval-bench on {{name}} was reinstalled and is now {{version}}. You can run a benchmark now.
setup.installedNow: tool-eval-bench {{version}} is installed on {{name}}. You can run a benchmark now.

quality.diffSuite: These runs used different item sets (suite v{{a}} vs v{{b}}), so items with the same id are not the same question. Re-run one of them to compare.
